question: T12 (task-c272a67694f09f1e, task-85f10d5318d977a9, task-831fd329f46e1643): what a Cmd+Z that takes a Scrolling block's Wave Intensity back up does to the rows when the block is taller than its line, when it takes back a desktop step in the phone view, and whether a desktop move after a phone Cmd+Z refit moves the phone blocks. On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it, made on the desktop (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10, phone 1/2/3/10 and 3/2/5/10). Select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design, presses on Wave Intensity (179 is the press for 180), Escape and a press on the page (go), Cmd+Z ('z'). G1 (CAP-T12BELOW g, then more): in the phone view 180, 150, 120, go, one Cmd+Z, Desktop View, the Text block moved down one row by ArrowDown (select, key, Escape), Mobile View, Desktop View. G2: on the desktop 180, 150 (a fall), go, Mobile View, Cmd+Z twice, Desktop View. G3: in the phone view the Scrolling block made 1/2/12/10 by its handle (scripts/oracle/ui.mjs place, which may take more than one step), then 150, 90, go, Cmd+Z three times, Desktop View. Exit without saving each time. Read twice (R1 in the order G2, G1, G3; R2 G1, G2, G3), alike.
readsAre: As CAP-T12HELD: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' holds each drag's quick reads (states: [name, { t: the page's clock, L: the layout as in reads, st: value, focus (isRange: the range has it), Undo/Redo, selected blocks, lines, focus: the focused element by tag, type, label and role }]) and its events by the page's clock from the first (log: type, ms, pointer type, pointer id, target, the range's value). 'keys' holds the arrow key reads, as CAP-T12DRAGEND's. 'tapPoint' is the tap's point and what was under it; 'touchAction' the range's computed touch-action up its parents. The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built; 'z' always pressed).
answer: G1: g's first Cmd+Z gives the phone 1/2/7/10 and the Text block 7/2/9/10 (8 rows), as CAP-T12BELOW g. Then on the desktop ArrowDown moves the Text block from 1/2/3/10 to 2/2/4/10, and the phone areas stay: 1/2/7/10 and 7/2/9/10, 8 rows, in the phone view too. The desktop move does not move the phone blocks.

G2: a desktop fall 180 then 150 (1/2/7/26 to 1/2/6/26, the Text block kept at 5/2/7/10) leaves the phone areas as built (1/2/3/10, 3/2/5/10; the phone has no wave of its own and shows 150, its block 180 high over 4 rows). In the phone view a Cmd+Z that takes the fall back (desktop 1/2/7/26) gives the phone block the growth rows of 180: 1/2/8/10, the Text block 8/2/10/10, 9 rows. The next Cmd+Z gives the section as built.

G3: in the phone view a Scrolling block made 1/2/12/10 by hand (11 rows) keeps them at 150; the fall to 90 takes it to 1/2/10/10 (9 rows, the line's fall of 2 rows); the Cmd+Z that raises it back to 150 gives 1/2/12/10 and 11 rows again, the rows it had, not the fewer its line needs. The next Cmd+Z gives 1/2/7/10 (6 rows) and the next the section as built: the place by the handle took two steps there (not read which).
